utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Who is going first from the Defence teams? Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I begin my cross-examination and agree with the witness about the terms we're going to use, could we please go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you testified some time ago, you mentioned a man called Ejub Golic. Do you remember mentioning him and what you said about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I never knew this Golic man. When we came near Buljim on a first ambush, I saw that man there, but I wouldn't know who he was except that my neighbour told me he was next to last person to arrive there. This was a macadam road and the column was halted on that road. And then a young man came and said, "What are you waiting -- what are we waiting for?" And then he said that there was a stream, some 100 to 200 metres ahead and that the trace of the column was lost. And he said -- and then he said, "I will find you the trace." And then I asked my neighbour, "Who is this?" And the neighbour said, "This is Golic." And he went to the man who was down there. I remained on the macadam road. And to the left of the hill we heard somebody shout, "What are they waiting for, mother fuckers" pardon me, and then the shooting started, people dispersed and I never saw Golic again. I went down a stream, as I told you earlier. I didn't know where I was going. We went down that stream and there were both dead and wounded on both banks of that stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We should proceed slowly because we speak the same language. On that occasion, how many soldiers passed with Ejub Golic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: It was a long column. Ejub was next to last to arrive. I think that he was next to last to leave Jaglici. And as for Buljim, why they halted there, I don't know. I keep wondering to this day. When Ejub came, he said, "What are we waiting for?" And they said, "We lost the trace of the column down there." And then he said, "What are we waiting for?" and then cursed their mothers. And then all of a sudden, the shooting started on the left and on the right. People dispersed. Nobody paid attention to anybody else. Nobody paid attention to the wounded or to the dead. Everybody tried to save their own skin.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. At one point in time, were the people told to go to the right towards Siljkovici, Lolici, Sandici. Do you remember such an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I don't hear this from anyone. Perhaps, somebody heard such an order. I didn't. I'm just telling you about what I heard and what I saw. I came to that spot, to that macadam road with my next door neighbour and I learned from him that this was Ejub Golic. And once they started shooting, people dispersed and I never heard Ejub again after that. We went down the stream. It became dark. We turned to the left to a forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you this: You said that you came to the asphalt road and that some of the people from your group said that this village was called Lolici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I didn't get to the asphalt road. We were near Kamenica, outside of Kamenica when we were encircled and we surrendered there and then they forced us to go down to Lolici to the asphalt road. And the man who fled from the warehouse with me called me, told me that that place was called Lolici.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The meadow where you were, did he tell you that that was the village of Lolici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of the village of Sandici? Do you know where that village is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about that upon my return to Srebrenica. I filed various requests to have my property returned to me and I passed through Sandici which is near Bratunac, but until that time, I had never seen that place. I heard that that area called Podbudje had a number of villages but I had never visited that area before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now that you passed through that region and that you saw the signs saying Sandici, do you still remain by your statement that you were in the village of Lolici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I didn't know whether it was Lolici or Sandici or Hrncici or something else. It's just that he had told me, this is what he said, that we were in Lolici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The procedure here is that what you are saying in your own language and what Mr. Stojanovic is saying in his own language needs to be translated to us into English and into French. So it is important that when Mr. Stojanovic finishes his question, putting his question, that you don't jump in and start answering the question straight away. You need to allow a short interval of time, a short pause, so that the interpreters can finish translating what Mr. Stojanovic would be saying. All right? Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, now could you give me an approximate estimate of time, from 20 to 1.00 when you arrived until you moved to Kravica, how long did you stay in Lolici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I didn't have a watch on me, but in my judgement, we sat there for four to five hours. Now, as to when we arrived, I don't know that either. I think that many a person would find it difficult to estimate the time as to exactly how long we stayed there and so on, because those were difficult moments.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this way: How long after Mladic's departure elapsed before you went to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: After Mladic's departure, we stayed less than half an hour, and then we set out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you were lined up and when you set out as you have described to us, did all of the prisoners set out from the meadow or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: When I set out, I was in the middle of the column, or thereabouts. And those behind me naturally set out too. When we reached a curve, I saw the front end of the column, and I think that they did set out, because they entered the warehouse after me, and the warehouse was full. So I guess nobody was left behind in the meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you testified down there sometime ago, you testified -- you described a man who was at the front end of the column, at the helm of the column, that he was of medium height, dark hair, a blue sweater and a jacket.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I didn't say a jacket. He was in civilian uniform. He had a dog on a leash. He had a machine-gun, either 53 or 84. I can't tell you exactly because he was at a distance from me. As for the jacket, I didn't see a jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was his face painted with black paint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: He had some kind of black grease. I -- I didn't put the grease on him. I could see what his eyes were like and his teeth.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I believe that it's hard to do that, and I'm just trying to help you by telling you what you said before. That man, did he order, after Mladic left, you to line up and to go to Srebrenica [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: He ordered that a column be formed, a column of four abreast like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps for the transcript, page 43, line 16, the witness and I said "to go to Kravica" but in the transcript it says "to go towards Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If we can agree, Witness, you said to go to Kravica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Well, no, no, not Srebrenica. I wasn't going towards Srebrenica, I was fleeing from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Thank you. You also said that the column was followed by another group of people in civilian clothing with weapons. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I didn't say anywhere in civilian clothing, as far as I can recall. But in military uniforms, everybody had automatic rifles on both sides of the columns. They all had ammunition belts, and they were carrying their weapons at the ready, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we can move to a private session for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you set off towards Kravica in the column that you described, were you tied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anyone that was tied.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And were you tied when you were sitting on the meadow at Lolici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: No. From what I recall, I didn't say that we were tied anywhere. When we were crossing the river, we had to place our hands behind our backs, behind our head, and this was something that the two soldiers who searched us told us to do when we were crossing the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say hands tied, you don't mean your hands are tied with a rope?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I think you told me you understood me properly, that I placed my hand behind my back, as I was told, nobody told me to do it. I hope you understood me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I understand you now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: You understood that a long time ago, but you're just getting on my nerves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let's calm down. All right. Witness, I can understand that you are not feeling that well, and that you get irritated sometimes. On the other hand, Mr. Stojanovic, like every our lawyer, is doing his duty here, and you need to understand that. He is trying to defend his client. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand completely the lawyer, but the lawyer also, the gentleman needs to understand me. Because I would like to ask the lawyer, had he been in my place, how he would have felt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic. I don't know if we need a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think I need to calm the waters a little bit. I think let's have a 10-minute break. In the meantime, you will both have an opportunity to think on what you have said and what has been happening. Witness, we are going to have a short break of 10 minutes. And then we will continue afterwards. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. --- Break taken at 11.27 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before we continue, I would really like to apologise once again if I disturbed you in any way, and I really want to tell you that it is my objective just to establish the real truth of what happened, and to eliminate any kind of inconsistencies that we have. I don't have any other intention.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next thing that I would like to ask you is if you can tell us, according to your best recollection, how long in time or in kilometres you went from that place where you were on the meadow to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you the exact times because I didn't have a watch when I set off or when I arrived. I can't even tell you how many kilometres it was. I really couldn't give you the exact time, how long we walked. Because I was afraid, all I was thinking is what would happen to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you how long we travelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Then I'm going to ask you this: Earlier you mentioned that on the way to the warehouse you saw an APC, a UN APC?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it was approximately that you saw it? Was it close to the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't that far between Lolici and Kravica. It was closer to Kravica than to Lolici. It was on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was it following you or was it just standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: It was standing on the right-hand side. There were some soldiers standing around it, who they were or what they were, I don't know. They didn't react in any way. We passed by it and it stayed on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to show you a photograph that you had the opportunity to see earlier. I think that we can do it in e-court. PO2435. Maybe we can look at that and I would like to ask the usher to help us and to give the witness the marker so that he could mark what I asked him to on the photograph. When you see the picture on the screen I would like to ask you -- before you see that, I would like to ask you about the time, the moment you came in front of the Kravica warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Mr. Stojanovic, this document or this photo that you have chosen has markings in it, blue ink. What's your position on that, Mr. Vanderpuye? Do we have a clean one to start with? Because I think if we do we can cut this short and go to the clean one but I don't know the reference number.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Right, Mr. President. We don't have a clean version of this photograph. My understanding is this photograph was a photograph used in the state court proceedings and was disclosed to us or furnished to us in relation to the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, stop. Mr. Stojanovic, I suppose we can proceed, having heard that. Go ahead with your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps that can help us to be more efficient, because it's a photograph, and what is marked has been marked by the witness in the previous trial, and this is actually what my question is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this photograph in front of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. But it's not the same here as it was in the other photographs. It's a little bit tighter here, a bit more closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a photograph that you marked in the trial that is behind us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, I see what is marked in ink pen, but it's looking a bit different now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to guide you with my questions and maybe you can find your way around. Would it be true if I said that you came along this road where a line in ink pen has been drawn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I came from Lolici along this road. I see where the line has been drawn and I see the entrance as well that is marked with the pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, my question on that is as follows: There, where it's marked with the pen, is that where you turned to go towards the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, that is where we turned from the asphalt road to the warehouse, but there was a bus between the warehouse and the asphalt and we walked between the bus and the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to ask you to help us with the following: According to our information and exhibits that we were given, there is a wire fence here separating the road from the warehouse. I am now going to show you those documents and then we can see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: The fence wasn't there then. When I was going into the warehouse the fence wasn't there then.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you can then allow us to see it and then we can see about that. Your Honours, perhaps we can look at an excerpt from some footage we received from the Prosecution, V0002024. This is the time from 32 minutes 23 seconds to 32 minutes 49 seconds. So it's just 26 seconds long. And it is footage, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the conditions that I was coming in I did not see the fence. Whether it was put there before or after, I don't know. All I know is that I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, we are going to look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I think we need to decide on whether this should be redacted or not. I need to consult my colleagues of course. In lines -- let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We may proceed. We will not be using this exhibit any longer, except in this case. By your leave, I would like to put another photograph which is the closest one we have to the events timewise, and this is from the collection of Mr. Ruez. Could we please see Exhibit 4D74. In order to gain an idea of where this is located, we don't think that we can get anywhere further with this witness as to the exact location of the fence at the time. So we need 4D74, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If this is necessary, because the witness now has -- a while before he said there was. He has now told you that he never saw one, which leaves room for certain conclusions. Not having seen one doesn't mean there wasn't one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I will now conclude with this topic by putting another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we heard your answer. We are not expecting anything different from you. But now looking at this picture, the warehouse from a different angle, would you perhaps reconsider and tell us whether there might have been a fence at the time when you were there? Do you see the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, I see the warehouse, I see the road. I told you that I didn't see a fence. A fence did not exist at the time. And I can't say that I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I won't have any more questions about this. Thank you for your assistance, Your Honours. Now I would like to ask you this, Witness: As you were walking towards the warehouse, and as you were entering the warehouse, in the nearby hills and around the warehouse, did you hear any shooting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes. We could hear the shooting while we sat there around the hills, and then there was the tank that I told you on the left. It fired towards the forest. They were telling him that people from Srebrenica were in the forest, so he fired at the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I want to ask you next is the moment when the shooting started. As I understood your testimony, when the last man entered through the same door through which you had entered, and when he was actually unable to enter --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: No, no, he did enter but there was nowhere for him to sit down. The guy told him to sit down, ordered him to sit down, and kicked him. And he turned towards him and said, "See, there is no where for me to sit down." And then he shot a burst of fire into him and this is when the shooting started and I just bent my head down and the shooting continued all the way to the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you how long in your estimate that lasted when you say until the night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: As we entered the warehouse, and I didn't tell you what time it was when I entered, it was in the afternoon, perhaps 3.00, 4.00 p.m., perhaps even 5.00. And they were shooting until it became dark. When it became dark, the shooting ceased.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the course of that night, I'm now referring to the night between the 13th and the 14th, was there a lull?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: There was a lull during the night. There was no shooting. We can hear them talking, laughing in front of the warehouse, but there was no shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you didn't know who were the shoulder -- the soldiers who fired in the prisoners because you were unable to see that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see them, so I can't identify anyone. I can't point to a person and say, Well, this person shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At one point you said that you heard a noise of a heavy machinery on the following day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, the 14th. I wouldn't be able to tell you the time of the day because I didn't go out. Or rather, once I went out, I never went back. So I don't know what time of the day it was when the machinery noise was produced. I couldn't see the sun.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you give us some idea, was is it in the morning or in the afternoon on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Around noon. It could be that the noise started around noon. Before that they said, "Is there anybody healthy, and if so, come out." And we heard --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I will interrupt you. Let us go into private session for a moment because we are about to mention a name. Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: (redaction) (redaction)

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned at some point, sir, that the brothers who you named left towards Potocari from your village, and that there is -- nothing else is known about them. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you, please, tell us what their age was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: My brother was older than I was by four years. My neighbour was only a year older than I am. And all of the others were older than they were. Nine of them went to Potocari. This cousin of mine was the youngest amongst them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: When your daughter informed you, were you told that the elderly people were going to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. We have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Sorry for the interruption. Who is going next? Madam Fauveau or Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic. We are finding out when we should have a break, considering that we have been sitting since 10.30 with that short interval.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I will be very brief, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will soon have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's being suggested that we take the break now. And can we restrict it to 20 minutes this time? 25 minutes because of the redaction, yes. 25 minutes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: First, I would like to ask you to clarify something. (redacted) (redacted) that you set off from Jaglici on the 12th of July at 20 to 1.00?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we need to redact straight away the name where he comes from on line 16 on page 61, please. Or you need to delete from line 15, "You said..." right up to that comma. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. Sorry, I thought that was...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could we just go into private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Previously, I didn't ask to go into private session because I believed that this -- the fact of mentioning this name and time could not reveal the identity of the witness because there were about 20.000 people there, as it's been said. But I have nothing against us being in -- being in private session and dealing with this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But what I want to speak about is the following: Yesterday in the transcript, as I wrote down here on page 14, line 1, it was said that "he" set off from this place that I mentioned with that larger group at 20 to 1.00. So all I wanted to do was to ask the witness to clarify whether this was 20 to 1.00 in the afternoon or 20 to 1.00 at midnight, after midnight.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: It was 20 to 1.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Another thing I would like to ask you to clarify. You said, referring to Golic, whom you did not know before then, that he left before last. So could you, please, clarify when you mean that he left one but last. Was that him personally or do you mean the group of people that he was leading, the group of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: I think that his group was the last to set off from Jaglici, from what I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Reading your previous statements and listening to your testimony today, I got the impression that from the place where you set off until -- up to the place where you were captured, you came up against two ambushes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The first ambush was next to this place called Buljim where I saw Golic. And that's where the people ran off and then the second ambush was when we came up to a river I was with a neighbour of mine, together with him the whole time. There was some shouting that started up there under this one hill. A group of us, seven or eight of us, decided to go towards the place where we could hear all these people. Almost it got dark on the ground, and then up there when they started shouting, you didn't know what was -- who was shooting, what was going on. All we know is that we were being hit by a Praga from a neighbouring hill. It was like fire flies. And then we went back down the slope again and there were bursts of fires and I realised that I couldn't escape. So I just found this tree and I lay down next to this fallen tree and I thought that they were there too. There was firing, firing, firing, and when it stopped, I got up. I kept calling out them by their names. None of them were there when I stood up. I saw that I didn't have a -- any more -- a cap on my head. To this very day, I don't know what happened to it. Sometimes there would be a burst of fire. I went up there towards them. I said, Don't fire, it's our people. He said, Who is it? I said my name. And he told me his name up there. Wait for me there, and I went to the woods. I found that young man whom I had told to wait for me. I sat down next to him. I had a back-pack. I had bread. I had some meat. You have something in your back-pack. I do. You want to eat. I do. And he ate. Let's go. We got up. Then you had to step over dead bodies. Then you could hear from down there shouts, "Help, brothers." Five or six people went down there. There were bursts of fire. Nobody was coming back from down there, and we were with those wounded all night. There were wounded. There were dead. They said that the wounded had to be taken up to some hill, to some Kamenica. And then in the morning when I got out in into the hill, I don't know where these Kamenicas were. I noticed one of my people from the neighbouring village, a man, he was lining people up. I came up past them. They stayed on my left side. And these were people from the neighbouring village, practically my neighbours. They said, Let's go down this hill to Suceska. We passed some 500 metres from there and we found a large group of people. The male nurse was there. He was dressing people's wounds. There were many people from my village; quite a lot of them. I felt it was a little bit easier because I could see my neighbours were there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I understand -- yes, everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, I hate to stop you because I know that you have a story to tell. However, if we continue like this you are going to be here for days at length. The question was a very simple one. I mean Mr. Zivanovic asked you whether there were two ambushes during the time you left from the place where you set off until the place where you were captured. And your answer should have been, Yes, there were two or there was one or there were more than two and that's it. We didn't -- we didn't really need all this information. If you continue like this, you are going to be here today, tomorrow, the day after tomorrow, next week. I mean, we are trying to do our best to let you go home the earliest possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I did say that there were two ambushes from Jaglici to the place where I was captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I wanted to ask you now is, in both those ambushes there were many killed and wounded from the group that you were moving in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One other thing. I think today we will be stopping a little bit earlier. There has just been an announcement that the weather is getting worse and we are letting everyone go home as soon as possible. So I think we will stop at 1.30, around 1.30 or thereabouts, depending on where we stand at the time. Everyone should be leaving here by 2.00. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic. Sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I read the statement that you gave to the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is the state commission for gathering information about war crimes. This was on the 21st of September, 1995. In the statement, I'm going to read just one sentence that has to do with victims in the second ambush. This is at Bratunacka Kamenica where you say, "It seems to me that there were 500 corpses and there were countless wounded. We had to walk over the bodies." Do you recall that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that very well. You couldn't count anybody -- nobody could count them that night, not the dead nor the wounded. They were lying there like logs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And was the first -- this situation the same with the first ambush?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: There were fewer dead and wounded there. I saw fewer dead and wounded there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Who is next? Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Meek. Who is next? Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you join the ABiH army in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You were demobilised in 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: [French on English channel]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you were in Srebrenica before the fall of the enclave, [No interpretation] THE FRENCH INTERPRETER: Would Madam Fauveau kindly repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, could you kindly repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, you have already answered, but for the transcript, I'm asked to ask the question again. Can we say that when you were in the Srebrenica enclave, before the fall of the enclave, you were under the command of Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, do you know where the headquarters of the unit of which Zulfo Tursunovic was a commander? Do you know where that headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: What -- what headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know where was the seat, the headquarters of the unit of which Zulfo Tursunovic was a commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: The seat, his seat was in the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, let's cut this short. Are you telling us that there was no headquarters? No headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What headquarters? I don't know. That's where the command was. There was some kind of kitchen there where they were cooking for the soldiers, for the refugees who had fled from Vlasenica, Bratunac, Rogatica. They didn't manage to sow anything, so they had to feed them and there was some sort of kitchen there and a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And where was this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Suceska, in the hills, that's where the kitchen was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it right to say that the 11th of July 1995 you received an information through a messenger that Srebrenica had fallen and that the women and children as well as the elderly were to go to Potocari while the others were to go to the forest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, I was informed, and I think I said that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This information, you got it from your commander Zulfo Tursunovic and he told you to establish a corridor towards Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you left to Jaglici, is it right to say that the men separated from their families at Ravni Gore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Ravne Njive, not Ravne Gore. It's above the village of Ravne Njive.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this precision. My mistake. Is it right that when you left to Jaglici on the 11th of July, 1995 you had a rifle with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Yes, I had my hunting rifle. I was a hunter.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you were wearing civilian clothes, right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct that before the fall of the Srebrenica enclave -- thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Yes, one moment. Page 68, please, lines 6. Now, in various instances where Zulfo Tursunovic's -- Zulfo Tursunovic was mentioned by name, we don't have it in the transcript. So that's for the record. But then the only place where supposedly he is mentioned in line 6 of page 68 he is wrongly mentioned as Zulfo Salilovic, when in actual fact Madam Fauveau clearly stated Zulfo Tursunovic. So that is to be corrected. And the same occurs on line --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zulfo Salilovic was in the warehouse where I was for the execution. (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We were talking of Zulfo Tursunovic here and on line 24 it is the same, in other words, Zulfo Salilovic has been substituted by Zulfo Tursunovic. Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We are in open session. I think the most recent remark that was made by the witness probably needs to be redacted. I know the Court's aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: His answer was not interpreted when Madam Fauveau asked whether he was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, we need to redact 20 and 21, please, of page 69. The last two words of line 21. That would suffice. Yes. And I thank Judge Kwon for drawing our attention that the witness has still got to answer the question. Madam Fauveau, I suggest that you repeat your question and then we will ask the witness to answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, once again, I have to repeat my question. Is it correct that you were wearing civilian clothes when you left to Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-156
utterances.text: Civilian clothing. I didn't have any military clothing. Maybe 10 per cent just had the military uniforms. Because we were almost all of us in civilian clothes, only a small number wore military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, you just answered my following question, so I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau. Who is next? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We have no questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Josse? Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Likewise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Nor us, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there re-examination, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, there is not, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't have any further questions for you, sir, which means that your testimony has come to an end. I wish to thank you for having come over to give evidence. And on behalf of the Tribunal, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you for making it possible to learn the truth about the genocide of Bosniaks in protected Srebrenica, and everyone should visit the cemetery in Potocari. That is the key evidence. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You can escort the witness out of the courtroom. Now, yesterday's witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make an assessment of how much time we require to conclude the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe 15 minutes, Mr. President, for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And after you, who is left? Who wishes to cross-examine yesterday's witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Everyone is being very shy --

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will not have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We wouldn't have any questions for this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Nor we, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I think is finished. And Mr. Josse.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We've had our go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's finish with this witness. The only problem is I don't know if he will be able --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Would you like to deal with the tender issue after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We can do the tendering now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I think the exhibits to tender have been disclosed to the Defence, yes. And...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have the list. Are there any objections on the part of the Defence teams to the admission of any of these documents? None. So they are so admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First one will remain under seal. Now, the Defence teams, Mr. Stojanovic, you made use of some documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since most of the documents that we used have already been tendered, we would just like to propose the footage, the video footage marked as 4D76 and that is video footage V002024, and if possible, we would like to have that segment to be admitted under seal for reasons that we have already stated and explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it needs to be under seal because the segment that you showed is in itself harmless. So I think it -- that segment which has already been identified first in the transcript will go -- do you have any objections, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I don't have an objection. I just wonder if the segment that's indicated here looks as though it's 32.23 through 32.49, if that's -- because I remember we froze the image at some point. I just wanted to make sure that they corresponded with one another. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. All right. So I think it is so admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And we will do the checking.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it shows that witness, then obviously that part won't show up. Yes, I see Mr. McCloskey standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have another witness that is also available after this one, if the Court wants to consider that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we will hear that witness today. So good afternoon to you, Witness. We are trying to finish with your testimony today. Madam Fauveau will cross-examine you and then I think you are free to go. Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, is it right that when you were in Zepa and when you heard that the civils -- civilians were to be evacuated, this is when you decided to go towards the mountains?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think there is something wrong. I mean it's -- his microphone is on. Wasn't it on before? All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just learned that the wounded were to go first. They would be the first to be evacuated. I learned that in the hospital where I was. That morning I went to the mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in the mountains where you left, were people who belonged to the Bosnia-Herzegovina army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them. I wasn't with them. There were some women, men, and less than a couple of them had any rifles. Those were people with their families. I stay there for a while. I ate with this friend of mine who was there, and then we went elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you said, it's on the page -- on page 30 of the transcript, "[In English] I decided with my colleague who was with me in the room, I decided to go to mountain where the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was up there, however, when I reached the mountain, I didn't see any army. Most likely they were in the forest and all over the mountain. It's a huge mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when you heard that a group of wounded had been evacuated, you came back to Zepa; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: It is correct that when you arrived in Zepa you had no ID on you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when you were in Srebrenica, before the fall of the enclave, you were a member of the 282nd Brigade of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you never wore a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And many members of the BiH army actually wore civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we move into private session for the following question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's move to private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday, my colleague asked you the question, I don't know whether you remember, but whether the Red Cross had observed the evacuation of civilians. And to that you answered that you did not remember. Do you remember having said that? This is a statement that is in the transcript on page 84.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember saying that. The Red Cross was only within the UNPROFOR compound. I didn't see them go to the civilians who were evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, my colleague, yesterday, showed you your statement in the Krstic case that was April of the year 2000. And my colleague, I'm not going to quote you again here, but he showed you the question which was asked to you, and your answer in which you said that the Red Cross actually watched over civilians being evacuated. So, my question is, do you remember having testified in the Krstic case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember stating that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: For the transcript, it's Krstic case...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it -- I understand what you mean, Ms. Fauveau because the transcript as it is might give the indication that the witness doesn't remember that he testified in the Krstic case, which I don't think is what he said. He is obviously referring to the detail from his alleged testimony that he doesn't remember. Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, will you allow me to say that, since you don't remember what you said in the year 2000 in the Krstic case, that you might not remember accurately the events of 1995 and that you might have forgotten that the Red Cross was actually watching over civilians being evacuated or the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you this. This was not far away from the UNPROFOR compound where I was and where the Red Cross was. Perhaps 200 to 300 metres, I'm not quite sure, and one could see the people from the UNPROFOR base, because there was a clear view of the road and the evacuation. One could see the buses. I don't know what the role of the Red Cross was though, whether they observed the evacuation, why they had come there. Perhaps they had come there just to register us. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we move to closed session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's do that; let's move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: When you were waiting to be evacuated from Zepa, you spent two nights outside the UNPROFOR bases in a house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Who was with you in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could you freely enter and exit the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the evening or during the day?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At any time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at night. We were not allowed. During the day, yes, we were moving about. At night there were UNPROFOR guards. There was an armoured vehicle there, I don't know which one, in front of our entrance on the road. The vehicle was parked there the whole night.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned the commander of the brigade Avdo. Is it correct that when you reached the territory under the control of the Bosnia and Herzegovina government, that Avdo was seen after the fall of Zepa?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. This is calling for speculation on this witness. There is no foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the question needs to be rephrased. I mean, we can understand Mr. McCloskey's objection. However, it's a legitimate question that needs to be rephrased and basically I'm going rephrase it myself. Witness, when you reached the BiH territory, did you yourself see Avdo, the Avdo that you mentioned yesterday, after the fall of Zepa, or are you aware of anybody else seeing Avdo alive at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see him. When the wounded were evacuated, he remained within the UNPROFOR compound and I don't know anything about his fate following that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown Exhibit 2D57, page 4. I would like to -- that this document be not -- not be circulated. THE FRENCH INTERPRETER: Correction, not be put on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right, not broadcast -- THE FRENCH INTERPRETER: Broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It needs to be put on the screen, but it must not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, at the end of the second paragraph you said, and this is the statement you made to the Prosecutor's office dated November 26th, 1998, "[In English] I heard later on the -- free territory that some prisoners detained in Batkovic prison camp near Bijeljina had seen Avdo being detained there. As far as I know, no one ever saw him since the war is over and he is presumed dead." [Interpretation] Does this bring back any memories?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Object to the form of these questions unless the -- Madam Fauveau will put her case to the witness. Is she suggesting that Avdo Palic is alive, and if so, I think she should put their case to the witness, otherwise, what is the relevance of this gossip?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Fully agreed. Yes, Madam Fauveau, I think you need to bring your questions -- or realign your questions to what Mr. McCloskey has just objected to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, to answer to Mr. McCloskey, I'm not suggesting Avdo Palic is alive and that's not actually what is suggested in what I just read out. I am just suggesting that he might have been seen there after and this is what is said in the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I think he's given you an answer and I don't think that's going to change. So let's proceed to the next subject or further questions that you might have.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, when you were -- when you were in Srebrenica, when you were part of the 282nd Brigade, can you tell me where this brigade was headquartered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The headquarters was in the hotel Domavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And was this hotel located in the centre of Srebrenica? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much more time do you require?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just have one other question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we all know where the hotel Domavia is and you can proceed to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is the unit you were part of, and here I'm talking about your particular unit, not the brigade but the smaller unit, had there -- had this unit a place where it would meet to discuss the military situation and receive orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And can you tell me where this particular place was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-111 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to say that. I don't want to say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there re-examination, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Just a housekeeping matter, Judge. I believe page 82, starting at line 2, with Mr. McCloskey's objection, which ended on line 5, he says "otherwise what is the relevance of this gossip," and the transcript said, "what is the basis for this gossip." I frankly agree with him that gossip shouldn't be around, but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I agree with you too, so I think that's a point. Thank you for the point that you have made. Witness, we don't have any further questions for you which means you are free to go. I wish to thank you on behalf of the Tribunal for having come over to give testimony in this case and I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have just one question if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, Your Honours, the Defence counsel who cross-examined me yesterday, who was the first to cross-examine me yesterday, there's something that's unclear to me about it. Since I have the status of a protected witness here, I don't know whether my name first and last name, the name of my father, may be revealed here publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't need to trouble yourself with this. It was not revealed publicly, and none of the information that is relevant to you, your identity or your family's identity were dealt with in open session. Everything was in private session. So you don't need to worry about that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday, the gentleman who was the first to cross-examine me, yesterday, stated my first and last name and my father's name publicly. This is why I put this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was not in public, it was in private session, if at all -- if the names were mentioned. But it was in private session. So it's not public.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow. Shall we do them now or tomorrow? Prosecution lists of exhibits has been circulated. Are there any objections on the part of any of the Defence teams? We hear none. So they are all admitted. The ones that are indicated to be preserved under seal will be kept under seal. I understand that the Borovcanin Defence team wishes to tender one document, and that's 4D73. Is that correct? Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there any objection on the part of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, but Ms. Stewart tells me that document 1516 was -- 1563 was already admitted through another witness, so that shouldn't be on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You can deal with that with our Registrar, and she will take care of that. So 4D73, which is not opposed, objected to by the Prosecution will also be admitted. I take it that this has been translated into English, hasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So this is admitted. We stand adjourned. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just one point. I think everyone knows, we have two more intercept operators that we obviously would like to get done tomorrow. I think we should be able to do that as well, but I hope Holland can handle a little snow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's hope that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a -- one issue. I believe that these 4D73 should be under seal because the witness indicated just that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you for pointing that out. And that will be under seal. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I just saw my name on the transcript this morning. I don't know if you had confirmation yet about your query. I checked that witness for whom delayed disclosure was ordered. The disclosure was made in hard copy last November, and if anybody didn't get it, they can tell me, but I haven't heard that. And the date we were thinking of, and I will discuss this with my colleagues, for that particular witness is the 26th of February, not the 27th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just need a confirmation that everyone has received a copy of the witness statement in November as stated. That's all. Because we want to make sure that the 30-day time period is strictly observed. So we stand adjourned. And I suggest -- recommend that you take the advice that everyone has been given to go home the earliest, because the storm is bound to get worse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
